unit: science / physics-paper-2 (Unity College, AQA Combined Science: Trilogy)

findings.claim: Getting this distinction right is essential for the exam - AQA regularly tests whether students can classify quantities correctly.
findings.truth: The board must never be named in student-facing text. Reworded to 'questions often ask you to classify quantities correctly'.
findings.evidence: house rule (Eduqas/WJEC neutral phrasing extended to all boards)

findings.claim: Card 3 answer 'force'; its question reads 'A push or pull acting on an object, measured in newtons (N). Forces are vectors - they have both size and direction.'
findings.truth: The answer word appears in the question, so the card gives itself away. Second sentence changed to 'It has both size and direction.'
findings.evidence: flashcard hygiene rule

findings.claim: Upthrust is taught as one of the contact forces to know.
findings.truth: Upthrust is correct physics but it belongs to Pressure and forces in fluids, which is separate-physics only (8463 6.5.5). It is extra, not wrong, so no edit.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.1.2 lists friction, air resistance, tension and normal contact force only

findings.claim: Beyond the limit of proportionality, the graph curves upwards - the spring extends more for each additional unit of force.
findings.truth: The lesson tells students to plot force on the y-axis against extension on the x-axis. Past the limit the extension grows faster than the force, so the gradient falls and the line bends towards the extension axis. The sentence contradicts its own next clause.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.3 force-extension relationship; recomputation of the gradient F/e past the limit

findings.claim: Cards 4 and 5 are auto-generated cloze fragments: answer 'Worked' for '_____ Example - Calculating Work Done A cyclist applies a force of 200 N...' and answer 'Step' for '_____ 1: Write the equation: W = Fs Step 2: ...'.
findings.truth: Both are junk cards scraped out of a collapsible. Replaced with real definition cards for limit of proportionality and spring constant. Answers stay unique in the deck and under 30 words.
findings.evidence: flashcard hygiene rule

findings.claim: v2 = 42 + 2(50) = 16 + 50 = 66. So v = sqrt(66) = 8.1 m/s (cyclist from 4 m/s at 0.5 m/s2 over 50 m).
findings.truth: The written substitution drops the acceleration: 2(50) reads as 100, not 50. The correct substitution is 2 x 0.5 x 50 = 50. The final answer 8.12 m/s is right.

findings.claim: The specification requires you to know this distinction for.
findings.truth: The sentence is cut off mid-thought. Full stop moved after 'distinction'.
findings.evidence: student-facing text

findings.claim: For objects undergoing uniform acceleration, AQA requires you to use this equation.
findings.truth: The board must never be named in student-facing text. v2 - u2 = 2as is also a given (equation sheet) equation rather than a recall one, but the lesson makes no recall claim, so only the board name is changed.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix B, second table, equation 1

findings.claim: Card 1 answer 'distance' with question ending 'Distance is a scalar quantity.'; card 2 answer 'displacement' with question ending 'Displacement is a vector quantity.'
findings.truth: Both answers appear in their own questions. Final sentences changed to 'It is a scalar/vector quantity.'
findings.evidence: flashcard hygiene rule

findings.claim: The area under a velocity-time graph is taught as core content (bullet n18), used in the worked example, in knowledge check 3 and in practice question 5, with no Higher flag. The tangent rule beside it IS wrapped in higher-only.
findings.truth: The spec marks the area under a velocity-time graph as HT only. Options: (a) wrap the bullet, the worked example and the two questions in higher-only, which is four separate places and will ripple into narration; (b) leave the teaching but add 'This is needed at Higher tier' to bullet n18 and to the practice question stem. I recommend (b) - one short sentence in each, no lost content for Foundation students.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.4.1.5: '(HT only) The distance travelled by an object (or displacement of an object) can be calculated from the area under a velocity-time graph.'

findings.claim: F = m x a ... This equation is on the AQA Physics equation sheet, but you must be able to rearrange it confidently.
findings.truth: F = m a is number 6 in the list of equations students must RECALL. The equation sheet carries only v2 - u2 = 2as, Ee = 1/2 k e2, E = m c dT, T = 1/f, F = B I l (HT), E = m L and Vp Ip = Vs Is (HT). Telling a student F = ma is given could cost them the whole question.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix B, both tables

findings.claim: Sitting on a chair: Your weight pushes down on the chair, and the chair exerts an equal upward normal contact force on you.
findings.truth: Weight acts on you and comes from the Earth; it is gravitational. The normal contact force is a contact force acting on you as well. They are not a third law pair, which the lesson itself states correctly three paragraphs earlier. The pair is: you push down on the chair, the chair pushes up on you.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.4.2.3 Newton's Third Law; the lesson's own misconception box at n28-n29

findings.claim: Inertia is flagged as Higher tier inside the lesson but appears unflagged in key takeaway 1 and in practice question 1.
findings.truth: Inertia is HT only. The main teaching is correctly wrapped, so the leak is minor. Not edited.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.4.2.1: '(HT only) The tendency of objects to continue in their state of rest or of uniform motion is called inertia.'

findings.claim: You must learn this equation - it appears frequently in AQA exams.
findings.truth: The board must never be named in student-facing text. Reworded to 'it is tested often'.
findings.evidence: house rule

findings.claim: In the exam, you may be asked to describe this required practical (the ruler-drop reaction time test).
findings.truth: The ruler drop is not a required practical on this course. The required practicals in these topics are 18 force and extension for a spring, 19 the effect of force and mass on acceleration, 20 waves in a ripple tank and in a solid, and 21 infrared absorbed or radiated by a surface. Reaction time appears only as an AT 1 skills opportunity. Changed to 'this experiment'.
findings.evidence: spec required practical activities 18-21; 6.5.4.3.2 lists reaction time under AT 1 only

findings.claim: Match question 5: right options are ['Braking distance', 'Thinking distance', 'Braking distance'] - options 0 and 2 are the same text.
findings.truth: The matcher marks by option index (js/main.js renderMatch), so a student who picks the other identical 'Braking distance' is marked wrong for a correct answer. Left item 3 changed to 'Higher speed' and right option 3 to 'Both thinking and braking distance', which is true and keeps order [0,1,2] correct.
findings.evidence: js/main.js renderMatch: 'if (parseInt(sel.value) === q.order[i])'; spec 6.5.4.3.1

findings.claim: F = change in momentum / time (F = dp/dt) is taught in n32-n34, restated in key takeaway 3 and is the whole subject of the 6-mark practice question.
findings.truth: The combined spec stops at p = m v and conservation of momentum, both HT only. Force as the rate of change of momentum, crumple zones and airbags are separate-physics (8463 6.6.3 Changes in momentum). Options: (a) cut n32-n34, the takeaway and question 6, which is a heavy narration edit; (b) keep the teaching as clearly-labelled extension but swap practice question 6 for a conservation-of-momentum question. I recommend (b) - a 6-mark extended response on off-course content is the part that actually misleads.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5.5 Momentum (HT only) has only 6.5.5.1 p = m v and 6.5.5.2 conservation of momentum

findings.claim: 'mechanical waves' is defined (in the dfn tooltip, the glossary and a flashcard) as 'A physical substance through which a wave can travel, such as air, water, or a solid.'
findings.truth: That is the definition of a medium, not of a mechanical wave. Lesson 10 carries the correct definition for the same term. Replaced with 'A wave that needs a medium (air, water or a solid) to travel through, such as a sound wave.' in all three places.
findings.evidence: spec 6.6.1.1; lesson 10 glossary entry for the same term

findings.claim: For example, if 10 crests span 30 cm, the wavelength is 30 / 10 = 3 cm (0.03 m).
findings.truth: Ten crests enclose nine wavelengths, so dividing by 10 is wrong. Changed to '10 wavelengths span 30 cm', which matches the sentence before it ('divide by the number of waves').
findings.evidence: recomputation: n crests span n-1 wavelengths

findings.claim: The required practical section covers only the ripple tank; required practical 21 (infrared) is not covered anywhere in the unit.
findings.truth: Required practical 20 is 'waves in a ripple tank AND waves in a solid'. Required practical 21 (how the infrared absorbed or radiated by a surface depends on its nature) sits in 6.6.2.2, so it belongs in this unit and is missing. Omission, not an error - no edit.
findings.evidence: spec required practical activities 20 and 21

findings.claim: In AQA Physics Paper 2, you will often be asked to compare different EM waves...
findings.truth: The board must never be named. The paper allocation itself is right: Physics Paper 2 covers topics 22-24, forces, waves, and magnetism and electromagnetism.
findings.evidence: spec Assessments, Physics Paper 2

findings.claim: The lesson explains why each EM wave type suits its application, and practice question 5 asks for explained comparisons, with no Higher flag.
findings.truth: Explaining suitability is HT only; Foundation students need the uses only. This over-teaches rather than misleads, so no edit.
findings.evidence: spec 6.6.2.4: '(HT only) Students should be able to give brief explanations why each type of electromagnetic wave is suitable for the practical application.'

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches moments (M = F d), the principle of moments, levers, gears and force as the rate of change of momentum, presented as Higher tier combined content (the body is wrapped in a higher-only block).
findings.truth: None of it is in the combined spec. Moments, levers and gears are separate-physics 6.5.2; changes in momentum is separate-physics 6.6.3. The higher-only wrapper is actively misleading - it tells a combined student this is Higher tier work they must learn. All 8 calculations in the lesson recompute correctly (420 x 1.6 = 672 Nm; 45 x 0.20 = 9.0 Nm; 71 x 25 = 1775 kg m/s; 1775/0.54 = 3287 N; 1775/0.35 = 5071 N, a 35% drop; 1200 x 15 = 18000, /0.60 = 30000 N, /0.20 = 90000 N). The diagram is served from separate-sciences/physics-separate/. Options: (a) move the lesson to the separate-sciences subject; (b) keep it but relabel the wrapper as extension beyond this course. I recommend (b) for Unity, since triple students share the class, with the label changed from Higher tier to 'beyond the combined course'.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5 Forces contents: no moments, levers or gears; 6.5.5 Momentum stops at conservation

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches the law of reflection, specular and diffuse reflection, plane mirror images, the hearing range and pitch/loudness, ultrasound, SONAR and seismic waves, wrapped in a higher-only block.
findings.truth: The combined spec covers only 'sound waves travelling through air are longitudinal' and a method to measure the speed of sound in air. Reflection is named once, as an HT statement that substances may absorb, transmit, refract or reflect. There is no law of reflection, no ultrasound and no seismic waves. All calculations check out (1600 x 0.35 = 560, /2 = 280 m; 1500 x 0.50 = 750, /2 = 375 m) and 330 m/s matches the spec's typical value. Same recommendation as F23: relabel as beyond the combined course, or move to separate sciences.

findings.claim: Description is 119 characters: 'The law of reflection, sound wave properties, ultrasound applications, and seismic wave evidence for Earth's structure.'
findings.truth: The validator limit is 100 characters. Shortened to 93 characters.
findings.evidence: house validator limit

findings.claim: In AQA Physics questions on waves for detection and exploration...
findings.truth: The board must never be named in student-facing text.
findings.evidence: house rule

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches convex and concave lenses, ray diagrams, magnification, colour and colour filters, specular/diffuse reflection and black body radiation. It is NOT wrapped in a higher-only block, so it reads as core content.
findings.truth: All of it is separate-physics: lenses and visible light are 8463 6.6.1.4-6.6.1.5, black body radiation is 8463 6.6.2.5. The only thing the combined course needs nearby is required practical 21, how much infrared a surface absorbs or radiates, which this lesson touches on only in one key fact. Recommend the same treatment as F23/F24, plus adding the required practical 21 method somewhere in the unit (see F20).
findings.evidence: spec 6.6 Waves contents: no lenses, no colour, no black body radiation

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches the generator effect, alternators and dynamos, microphones and loudspeakers, transformer construction and the turns-ratio equation Vp/Vs = np/ns, wrapped in a higher-only block inside a Paper 2 unit.
findings.truth: The combined spec's magnetism topic ends at 6.7.2.3 Electric motors. There is no generator effect, no induced potential, no alternator or dynamo, no microphone or loudspeaker, and no turns ratio. Transformers appear once, under 6.2.4.3 The National Grid, which sits in the Electricity topic and is therefore examined on Physics PAPER 1, not Paper 2 - and there the spec says 'Detailed knowledge of the structure of a transformer is not required', with the only Higher equation being Vp Ip = Vs Is (power), not the turns ratio. Both transformer calculations in the lesson are arithmetically correct (400 x 100/2000 = 20 V; 25000 x 10000/500 = 500000 V). Recommend relabelling as beyond the combined course and, if the National Grid part is kept, moving it to the Paper 1 unit.
findings.evidence: spec 6.7 contents and 6.2.4.3 The National Grid; Appendix B second table equation 7

findings.claim: 'potential difference' is defined (in the dfn tooltip, the glossary and a flashcard) as 'A voltage produced across a conductor when it experiences a changing magnetic field.'
findings.truth: That defines an induced potential difference, not potential difference. Replaced with 'The energy transferred per coulomb of charge between two points, measured in volts (V).' in all three places.
findings.evidence: spec 6.2.1.3 potential difference / settled definition

findings.claim: The whole lesson teaches the solar system, orbits, satellites, the life cycle of stars, red-shift, the Big Bang, dark matter and dark energy. Unlike lessons 9, 10 and 12 it is not inside any higher-only block, so it reads as core content for every student.
findings.truth: Space physics is separate-physics only (8463 6.8). None of it is examined on the combined course. Facts and figures all check out (4.6 billion years, 13.8 billion years, 1.4-3 solar masses, 2.7 K / -270 C, Penzias and Wilson 1965, 5/27/68 per cent, 1.5e11 / 3.0e8 = 500 s). Same recommendation as F23.
findings.evidence: spec 6.5-6.7 are the only physics topics; there is no space physics section

findings.claim: When the core reaches around 15 million degC, nuclear fusion begins - hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium, releasing enormous energy. At this stage the young star is called a protostar.
findings.truth: A protostar is the stage BEFORE fusion starts - the lesson's own glossary says 'a young, contracting star that has not yet begun nuclear fusion in its core'. The order was rewritten to nebula, protostar, fusion begins, main sequence star. Both dfn blocks and the narration block are kept.
findings.evidence: the lesson's own glossary entry; settled astrophysics

summary: Lessons 9 to 13 are wholesale separate-science content that is not on the combined spec at all (moments/levers/gears, reflection/sound/ultrasound/seismic, lenses/colour/black body, the generator effect/transformer turns ratio, and space physics) - five ADJUDICATE items, and three of those five hide behind a higher-only wrapper that tells a combined student the work is examinable. Lessons 1 to 8 are largely sound: the real errors are F = ma claimed as a given equation, a Newton's third law example that teaches the misconception the same lesson warns about, a force-extension graph said to curve the wrong way, and a wrong definition of 'mechanical waves' carried into the glossary and a flashcard. Every calculation in all 13 lessons recomputes correctly. 29 edits written.
